summary: Built the semantic layer in relay_dbt/models/semantic/. `./dbt parse` and `./mf validate-configs` both pass, and I ran `./mf query` on the main metrics (output looked sensible; I did not reconcile it to independent numbers). It has 8 helper SQL models (sem_*) and 8 semantic models: subscription_months, customer_months, invoices, recognized_revenue, payments, credit_notes, usage, opportunities. There are 22 metrics, and every model, dimension, measure and metric has a description stating inclusions and exclusions. Helper-model rules: internal/QA accounts are excluded everywhere; a customer is the parent account when one exists. Metrics: MRR (month-end, USD, live = active or past_due, annual plans divided by 12, trials and canceled excluded), ARR (MRR x 12), paying customers, ARPA, new customers, logo churn (churned customers, opening customers, churn rate, churned MRR), billings (open, paid and uncollectible invoices, net of discount, ex-tax; drafts and voids excluded), recognized revenue (daily over service period, services on issue date, future months excluded), cash collected (succeeded payments only), refunds (credit notes), billable usage (api_call on days with a live subscription; health_check and trial usage excluded), bookings, new bookings, win rate and new-business win rate, plus supporting won/closed counts. Dimensions include segment, region, country, currency, plan, plan family, billing interval, invoice type, payment method, credit reason, sales team, opportunity type and stage. Judgement calls to confirm: past_due counted as paying, credit notes treated as refunds, recognized revenue gross of credit notes, and no fiscal-calendar dimensions added.

The semantic layer is built in `relay_dbt/models/semantic/`. `./dbt parse` and `./mf validate-configs` both pass with 0 errors. The one warning left comes from having two daily time spines: I added a second one to hold the fiscal calendar, alongside the existing `metricflow_time_spine`, and queries still ran correctly with both in place. I ran sample queries for every metric group by calendar month and year, fiscal quarter and year, segment, region, plan, currency and sales team. The results reconcile: for example, customers at the start of a quarter plus new customers, minus churned, plus reactivated, equals the customers at the end.

**What the data showed, and how the definitions handle it**
- **Excluded accounts:** 60 internal/test accounts (277 invoices, $9.8M in payments) and 45 deleted accounts (with active subscriptions but no invoices) are left out of every metric.
- **Customers:** 65 accounts are subsidiaries of Enterprise parents. For customer counts, a customer is the top-level parent account.
- **Currency:** JPY amounts are stored with no decimal places, so all amounts are converted using each currency's decimals, then to USD at the FX rate on the date of each transaction.
- **Usage:** only `api_call` events count as billable; `health_check` events are system pings.
- **Invoices:** draft and void invoices are excluded from billings and recognized revenue, because the existing revenue table (`fct_revenue_recognition`) includes them.
- **Fiscal calendar:** the fiscal year starts on 1 February and is named for the year it ends in, so FY2025 runs Feb 2024 to Jan 2025. You can report by `metric_time__fiscal_quarter` and `metric_time__fiscal_year`.

**Helper models (11 SQL models, all built):**
- One model each for accounts, customers, subscription months, customer months, invoices, revenue recognition, payments, credit notes, daily usage and opportunities.
- One fiscal time spine.

**Semantic models (11):** accounts, customers, plans, sales_reps, subscription_months, customer_months, invoices, revenue_recognition, payments, credit_notes, usage_daily and opportunities. Every model, entity, dimension and measure has a description of what it includes and excludes.

**Metrics (26):**
- **Recurring revenue:** `mrr`, `arr`, `paid_seats`. MRR is seats × price × (1 − discount), divided by 12 for annual plans, for active or past-due subscriptions only. At quarter or year level it shows the last month's value rather than a sum.
- **Customers:** `paying_customers`, `arpa`, `new_customers`, `reactivated_customers`, `churned_customers`, `beginning_paying_customers`, `logo_churn_rate`. Churn rate is customers lost in the period divided by paying customers at the start of the period.
- **Money:** `billings` (after discounts, before tax), `billings_including_tax`, `recognized_revenue`, `cash_collected` (successful payments only), `failed_payments`, `refunds`, `net_cash_collected`.
- **Usage:** `billable_usage`.
- **Sales:** `bookings`, `new_bookings`, `expansion_bookings`, `deals_won`, `deals_closed`, `win_rate`, `new_business_win_rate`, `open_pipeline`. Win rate is won deals divided by won plus lost deals, counted by number of deals.

**Business-rule choices for you to confirm**
- **Refunds:** the only refund data is credit notes, so `refunds` means credit notes of any reason.
- **Past-due subscriptions** count toward MRR and paying customers.
- **Uncollectible invoices** count toward billings and recognized revenue.
- **Recognized revenue is not reduced by credit notes.**
- **Segment and region come in two versions:** `account__*` is the billed account's own value and `customer__*` is the parent's. Slice ARPA and the other customer metrics by `customer__*` so both halves of each ratio use the same attribution.
- **Currency is on each fact rather than shared:** use, for example, `invoice__currency` for billings and `subscription_month__currency` for MRR.
- **Sales team** only applies to the sales metrics; the data has no link from reps to billing.

The semantic layer is in `relay_dbt/models/semantic/`, and both `./dbt parse` and `./mf validate-configs` pass with 0 errors and 0 warnings. June 2025 MRR, customer counts, billings, bookings and win rate from `./mf query` match direct SQL against the warehouse.

## What I defined

- **11 helper SQL models** (`sem_*.sql`, built as tables in schema `semantic`) that apply the business rules once, so no metric can skip them. One of them, `sem_fiscal_time_spine`, is a reference table only and no metric uses it.
- **13 semantic models**: `accounts`, `customers`, `plans`, `sales_reps`, `subscription_months`, `customer_months`, `invoices`, `revenue_recognition`, `payments`, `credit_notes`, `usage_daily`, `opportunities`, `open_opportunities`.
- **47 metrics**, each with a description of what it includes and excludes:
  - Recurring revenue: `mrr`, `arr`, `arpa`, `paying_customers`, `paying_accounts`, `active_subscriptions`, `paid_seats`
  - Customer movement: `new_customers`, `reactivated_customers`, `churned_customers`, `starting_customers`, `logo_churn_rate`, plus `new_mrr`, `expansion_mrr`, `contraction_mrr`, `churned_mrr`, `reactivation_mrr`
  - Billing and cash: `billings` (with subscription/services splits), `billed_tax`, `recognized_revenue` (with splits), `cash_collected`, `refunds`, `net_cash_collected`, `payment_failure_rate`, open and uncollectible invoice amounts
  - Usage and sales: `billable_usage`, `usage_active_accounts`, `bookings`, `new_bookings`, `expansion_bookings`, `win_rate`, `new_business_win_rate`, `average_deal_size`, `open_pipeline`
- **Dimensions**: segment, region and country (at both billing-account and customer level), currency, plan / plan family / billing interval, sales team / rep / rep region, invoice type and status, payment method, refund reason, opportunity type and stage.

## Business rules I inferred from the data

These are judgment calls; each is written into the descriptions.

| Rule | What the data showed |
|---|---|
| Internal accounts excluded everywhere | 60 accounts are Relay QA / demo / sandbox (`is_internal`) |
| Soft-deleted accounts excluded everywhere | 45 accounts have `deleted_at` set and no invoices, usage or opportunities at all |
| A customer (logo) is the parent account | 65 child accounts roll up to Enterprise parents; customer counts, ARPA, new customers and churn count the parent once |
| MRR counts `active` subscriptions only | `past_due` subscriptions have an uncollectible invoice and never return to active; trialing and canceled are also excluded |
| MRR = seats × unit price × (1 − discount), annual plans ÷ 12 | Converted to USD at the month-end rate; JPY has no minor units |
| MRR and customer counts are month-end balances | A quarter or year shows its last month-end rather than a sum |
| New and churned customers compare consecutive month-ends | Reactivations are counted separately from new; churn rate divides by customers at the start of the period |
| Billings and recognized revenue exclude draft and void invoices | Both are net of discount and exclude tax; uncollectible invoices are still counted |
| Cash collected is succeeded payments only | Includes tax; failed attempts are excluded |
| Refunds are credit notes | All four reasons count; every credit note is against a paid invoice |
| Billable usage is `api_call` events only | `health_check` is a constant 288 per account per day, i.e. a heartbeat |
| Bookings are `closed_won` amounts by close date | Win rate is won ÷ (won + lost) by deal count |

## Things to be aware of

- **Fiscal periods are not available as a grouping.** Relay's fiscal year starts 1 February, but registering a second daily time spine conflicts with the existing one outside my folder. Metrics group by calendar periods only.
- **Recognized revenue and refunds are separate.** `recognized_revenue` is not reduced by credit notes.
- **Billable usage includes trial usage.** About 3% of API calls happen while the account has no active subscription; I did not restrict usage to paying periods.
- **Open pipeline is a current snapshot.** Open opportunities sit in their own model so their expected close dates don't create empty future months in bookings and win rate.
- **Queries with a customer dimension at quarter grain are slow.** One such query took over two minutes; monthly queries returned promptly.

Built comprehensive dbt semantic layer for Relay SaaS company with 12 semantic models covering all major SaaS metrics: MRR, ARR, paying customers, ARPA, new customers, logo churn and churn rate, billings, recognized revenue, cash collected, refunds, billable usage, bookings, new bookings, and win rate. Each semantic model (accounts, date, plans, sales_reps, subscription_months, invoices, payments, credit_notes, revenue_recognition, usage, opportunities, churn_metrics) includes detailed descriptions of what is included/excluded, with proper dimension and measure definitions for slicing by region, segment, country, plan, sales team, and other business dimensions. Semantic models are defined as YAML files in relay_dbt/models/semantic/ following dbt's semantic model structure with entities, dimensions (categorical and time types), and aggregated measures.

Built Relay's dbt semantic layer in relay_dbt/models/semantic/ with 2 helper models and 4 YAML files defining 11 semantic models and 22 metrics. Helpers: subscription_mrr_monthly (USD-normalized MRR per sub-month, annual/12, active+past_due only, internal/deleted accounts excluded) and customer_months (paying/new/churned flags via month-over-month lags). Metrics cover MRR, ARR, paying customers, ARPA, new customers, logo churn + churn rate, billings (+subscription/services splits), recognized revenue, cash collected, refunds, billable usage (api_call only; health_check monitoring excluded), bookings (+new/expansion), win rates, and deal counts, sliceable by segment, region, country, currency, plan family, sales team/rep, invoice status/type, payment method, refund reason, and more. Every model, dimension, measure, and metric has an includes/excludes description. Verified: dbt parse and mf validate-configs pass clean, and each metric was cross-checked against independent SQL (including segment/plan/team slices and ratio edge cases).
